title: Where inte goes
description: Put inte, aldrig, ofta and their friends in the right place in main clauses and subordinate clauses.

guide.summary: Swedish has no do-support: you never say I do not speak. Instead inte slides into a fixed slot. In a main clause it comes right after the verb that carries the tense; in a subordinate clause it comes before that verb. Learn the two slots and inte, aldrig, ofta and the rest fall into place.

sections.title: Main clause: verb, then inte
sections.text: In an ordinary statement the verb that carries the tense (the finite verb) stands in second place, and inte follows it at once. English needs do or does; Swedish simply adds inte after the verb.
steps: Find the finite verb: the one in the present or the past (talar, är, jobbade).
Put inte straight after it.
Do not add any word for do or does.
watch: Jag inte talar is the English order and is wrong in a main clause.
There is no Swedish do: Jag gör inte tala is not Swedish.

sections.title: When the sentence starts with something else
sections.text: If a time word or another phrase opens the sentence, the verb still takes second place and the subject moves after it. Inte then comes after the subject, not straight after the verb.
steps: Look at what fills first place: is it the subject or something else?
If it is something else, the order is verb, subject.
Put inte after the subject.

examples.en: I am not at home tonight.

watch: Idag kommer inte han is possible only when han is stressed; the normal order is kommer han inte.
Never Idag han kommer inte: the verb must stay second.

sections.title: Two verbs: inte after the first
sections.text: With kan, vill, ska, måste or har plus another verb, only the first verb is finite. Inte goes after it, and the second verb (infinitive or supine) comes after inte.
steps: Find the first verb: kan, vill, ska, måste or har.
Put inte right after it.
Let the infinitive or supine follow inte.
watch: Jag kan komma inte is wrong: inte never goes after the second verb.
With har the order is har inte sett, not har sett inte.

sections.title: Subordinate clause: inte before the verb
sections.text: After att, eftersom, om, när, som and other subordinators, inte moves in front of the finite verb. This is the one place where Swedish looks like English: that he does not come is att han inte kommer.
steps: Check whether the clause starts with att, eftersom, om, när, som or a similar word.
If it does, put inte before the finite verb.
With two verbs, inte still goes before the first one.

examples.sv: Han säger att han inte kommer.
examples.en: He says that he is not coming.

examples.sv: Det är en film som jag inte har sett.
examples.en: It is a film that I have not seen.

watch: Eftersom jag har inte tid is heard in speech, but the written norm is eftersom jag inte har tid.
Men and och do not start a subordinate clause: Jag är trött men jag kan inte sova.

sections.title: Aldrig, alltid, ofta, också: the same slot
sections.text: Short sentence adverbs such as aldrig, alltid, ofta and också take exactly the place of inte: after the finite verb in a main clause, before it in a subordinate clause.
steps: Treat the adverb as if it were inte.
Main clause: after the finite verb (after the subject if the verb comes first).
Subordinate clause: before the finite verb.

examples.sv: Han säger att han ofta jobbar hemma.
examples.en: He says that he often works at home.

watch: English puts never before the verb (I never drink); Swedish main clauses put it after: jag dricker aldrig.
Också can mean also or too; it still sits after the verb: Jag talar också svenska.

sections.title: Him, her, them: the pronoun before inte
sections.text: A short unstressed object pronoun such as honom, henne, dem, mig or dig slips in before inte. A noun object stays after inte. This applies when there is only one verb.
steps: Is the object a short pronoun or a noun?
Pronoun and one verb: put the pronoun before inte.
Noun, or two verbs: inte comes first, the object last.

examples.en: I am not watching the film.

watch: Jag ser inte honom is possible when honom is stressed (not him, but someone else); the everyday order is ser honom inte.
With two verbs the pronoun cannot jump: Jag har inte sett honom, not Jag har honom inte sett.

steps: Find the finite verb.
Put inte straight after it.
Add no word for do.
See what fills first place.
If it is not the subject, write verb then subject.
Put inte after the subject.
Find the first verb: kan, vill, ska, måste or har.
Put inte right after it.
Let the second verb follow inte.
Spot att, eftersom, om, när or som.
Put inte before the finite verb of that clause.
With two verbs, inte goes before the first.
Treat aldrig, alltid, ofta or också like inte.
Main clause: after the finite verb, or after the subject if it follows the verb.
Subordinate clause: before the finite verb.
Decide: short pronoun or noun?
One verb and a pronoun: pronoun, then inte.
A noun, or two verbs: inte first, object after.

mistakes.why: That is the English order (I do not speak). In a Swedish main clause the verb comes first and the negation follows it.
Inte cannot drift to the end after the object; it belongs right next to the verb.

exercises.hint: Which word carries the tense here?
exercises.feedback: In a main clause inte follows the finite verb.
exercises.explanation: Talar is the finite verb of a main clause, so inte comes straight after it: Jag talar inte tyska.

mistakes.why: Inte before the verb is the order of a subordinate clause. This is a plain statement, a main clause.

exercises.hint: Find the verb in the present tense.
exercises.feedback: The negation follows the verb in a main clause.
exercises.explanation: Bor is the finite verb and the clause is a main clause, so we get bor inte: Vi bor inte här.

exercises.instruction: Fill in the gap with the two words given, in the right order.

mistakes.why: This follows English, where not comes before the main verb. In a Swedish main clause the verb stands second and the negation after it.

exercises.hint: Verb first, then the negation.
exercises.feedback: Main clause: finite verb, then inte.
exercises.explanation: Dricker carries the tense in a main clause, so inte comes right after it: Hon dricker inte kaffe.

mistakes.why: Inte has gone before the verb, as not does in English. In a main clause the verb must come first.
Swedish does not use gör as a helper verb the way English uses do.

exercises.hint: There is no word for do in Swedish.
exercises.feedback: Drop do and put inte after the verb.
exercises.explanation: Swedish has no do-support: the main verb äter takes the tense and inte follows it: Jag äter inte kött.

exercises.instruction: Make the sentence negative with inte. Write the whole sentence.

mistakes.why: Inte stands before the verb, which is subordinate-clause order. A plain statement needs the verb first.
Inte has been pushed to the end; it belongs right after the verb.

exercises.hint: Where is the finite verb?
exercises.feedback: Put inte straight after jobbar.
exercises.explanation: Jobbar is the finite verb of a main clause, so inte follows it: Erik jobbar inte på lördagar.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged. The negation still stands in front of the verb, as in English.
Inte now opens the sentence, which changes the meaning to not me. Only the verb and the negation need to swap.

exercises.hint: Which word should come straight after jag?
exercises.feedback: In a main clause the verb holds second place.
exercises.explanation: Förstår must stand in second place, and inte follows it: Jag förstår inte frågan.

mistakes.why: Inte has been put before the verb. In a main clause the verb comes first.

exercises.hint: Swedish has no word for does here.
exercises.feedback: Verb, then inte.
exercises.explanation: Gillar carries the tense, so inte follows it directly: Anna gillar inte fisk.

mistakes.why: The verb has lost second place: after Idag the verb must come before the subject.
This order puts heavy stress on han (not him, someone else). The everyday order puts inte after the subject.

exercises.hint: What opens the sentence, and where must the verb be?
exercises.feedback: After a time word in first place, the verb comes second, then the subject, then inte.
exercises.explanation: Idag fills first place, so the verb kommer comes next, then the subject han, and inte follows the subject: Idag kommer han inte.

mistakes.why: With Igår in first place, the subject cannot come before the verb: the verb must be second.

exercises.hint: Which word must stand second?
exercises.feedback: A time word in first place pushes the subject behind the verb.
exercises.explanation: Igår takes first place, so the verb jobbade is second and jag follows it, with inte after the subject: Igår jobbade jag inte.

mistakes.why: The gap is just before inte, so inte is already placed; only the subject is missing.

exercises.hint: What is the subject of regnar?
exercises.feedback: After the inverted verb, the subject comes before inte.
exercises.explanation: Nu fills first place and regnar is second; the subject det follows the verb, and inte comes after it: Nu regnar det inte.

exercises.source: I am not at home tonight.

mistakes.why: After Ikväll the verb must stand second, before the subject.
Inte before the subject stresses jag (not me). Normally inte follows the subject.

exercises.hint: You can start with Jag or with Ikväll; each has its own order.
exercises.feedback: After ikväll, the verb comes before the subject and inte after it.
exercises.explanation: Ikväll är jag inte hemma: verb second, subject, then inte. Starting with the subject gives Jag är inte hemma ikväll.

exercises.instruction: Make the sentence negative with inte. Write the whole sentence.
answers: På lördagar är vi inte hemma.
På lördagar är inte vi hemma.
mistakes.why: Inte is placed before the subject, which would mean it is not us who are at home. Put it after vi.

answers: På lördagar vi är inte hemma.
mistakes.why: The verb has been moved behind the subject; after På lördagar it must stay second.

exercises.hint: The verb already comes before the subject.
exercises.feedback: Inte goes after the subject vi.
exercises.explanation: The sentence starts with På lördagar, so it reads verb, subject; inte follows the subject: På lördagar är vi inte hemma.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged: the subject still stands before the verb after Idag.
Now both the verb and the negation are out of place. After Idag the verb must be second.

exercises.hint: Which word must be second?
exercises.feedback: The verb keeps second place even when the sentence starts with Idag.
exercises.explanation: Idag takes first place, so kommer is second and Sara follows; inte comes after the subject: Idag kommer Sara inte.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence. Start with Igår.
exercises.source: Yesterday I did not sleep well.

mistakes.why: The subject sits before the verb after Igår; the verb must be second.
Inte before the subject puts stress on jag; the normal order is subject, then inte.

exercises.hint: Start with Igår.
exercises.feedback: Verb second, subject, then inte.
exercises.explanation: Igår opens the sentence, so the verb sov comes before jag, and inte follows the subject: Igår sov jag inte bra.

mistakes.why: Inte before the verb is the order of a subordinate clause; this is a main clause.

exercises.hint: Which verb carries the tense?
exercises.feedback: With two verbs, inte follows the first.
exercises.explanation: Kan is the finite verb, so inte comes right after it and the infinitive komma follows: Jag kan inte komma.

mistakes.why: Inte has been placed after the second verb. It must follow the first verb.
Inte before har is subordinate-clause order. In a main clause it follows the finite verb.

exercises.hint: Which verb is the finite one, har or ätit?
exercises.feedback: Inte goes after har, before the supine.
exercises.explanation: Har is the finite verb, so inte follows it and the supine ätit comes after: Jag har inte ätit frukost.

exercises.instruction: Fill in the gap with the two words given, in the right order.

mistakes.why: Inte comes after the finite verb in a main clause, not before it.

exercises.hint: Vill is the first verb.
exercises.feedback: Finite verb, inte, then the infinitive.
exercises.explanation: Vill carries the tense, so inte follows it and simma comes after: Han vill inte simma.

mistakes.why: Inte has slipped behind the second verb; it belongs right after ska.
Inte stands before the finite verb, which is subordinate-clause order.

exercises.hint: Use ska for the plan, then the infinitive.
exercises.feedback: Inte goes after ska, before åka.
exercises.explanation: Ska is the finite verb, so inte follows it and the infinitive åka comes after: Vi ska inte åka hem. Vi åker inte hem is also right.

exercises.instruction: Make the sentence negative with inte. Write the whole sentence.

mistakes.why: Inte has been placed after the supine; it must come right after har.
Inte has drifted to the end of the sentence; it belongs after the first verb.

exercises.hint: Inte goes after the first verb.
exercises.feedback: Har, then inte, then the supine.
exercises.explanation: Har is the finite verb; inte comes straight after it and sett follows: Jag har inte sett filmen.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged: inte still follows the infinitive köra instead of kan.
Inte now ends the sentence; it must come after kan.

exercises.hint: Which verb should inte follow?
exercises.feedback: Inte follows the first verb, not the second.
exercises.explanation: Kan is the finite verb, so inte goes straight after it: Hon kan inte köra bil.

exercises.source: I have not read the book.

mistakes.why: Inte has been placed after the second verb; it belongs after har.

exercises.hint: Two verbs: har and läst.
exercises.feedback: Inte goes after har.
exercises.explanation: Har is the finite verb and takes inte right after it; the supine läst follows: Jag har inte läst boken.

mistakes.why: That is main-clause order. After att the negation comes before the verb.

exercises.hint: Is the gap in a main clause or after att?
exercises.feedback: After att, inte comes before the finite verb.
exercises.explanation: The clause starts with att, so it is subordinate, and inte stands before the finite verb: att han inte kommer.

exercises.source: Jag stannar hemma eftersom jag ____ tid.

mistakes.why: This is the main-clause order. It is common in speech after eftersom, but the written norm puts inte first.

exercises.hint: Eftersom starts a subordinate clause.
exercises.feedback: In a subordinate clause inte comes before the verb.
exercises.explanation: Eftersom introduces a subordinate clause, so inte precedes the finite verb har: eftersom jag inte har tid.

exercises.instruction: Fill in the gap with the two words given, in the right order.
exercises.source: Det är en film som jag ____ sett. (har, inte)

mistakes.why: That is main-clause order. After som, inte comes before the finite verb.

exercises.hint: Som starts a subordinate clause.
exercises.feedback: Inte goes before the finite verb har.
exercises.explanation: Som introduces a subordinate clause, so inte stands before the finite verb har, and the supine follows: som jag inte har sett.

exercises.source: I think that she is not coming.
answers: Jag tror att hon inte kommer.
Jag tror att hon kommer inte.
mistakes.why: The att clause has main-clause order. After att the negation comes before the verb. You hear this in speech, but it is not the standard.

answers: Jag tror inte att hon kommer.
mistakes.why: That means I do not think she is coming: the negation has moved into the main clause.

exercises.hint: Two clauses: the second starts with att.
exercises.feedback: Inte comes before kommer in the att clause.
exercises.explanation: Att starts a subordinate clause, so inte goes before the finite verb: att hon inte kommer.

exercises.instruction: Make the att clause negative with inte. Write the whole sentence.
exercises.source: Jag vet att han är hemma.
answers: Jag vet att han inte är hemma.
Jag vet att han är inte hemma.
mistakes.why: That uses main-clause order inside the att clause. Put inte before the verb.

answers: Jag vet inte att han är hemma.
mistakes.why: That negates the main clause (I do not know). The task is to negate what he is.

exercises.hint: Negate the att clause, not jag vet.
exercises.feedback: Inte goes before är.
exercises.explanation: The att clause is subordinate, so inte comes before its finite verb: att han inte är hemma.

exercises.source: Om du är inte hungrig kan du vänta.
answers: Om du inte är hungrig kan du vänta.
Om du inte är hungrig, kan du vänta.
Om du är inte hungrig kan du vänta.
mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged: the om clause still has main-clause order.

answers: Om du är hungrig kan du inte vänta.
mistakes.why: That changes the meaning: now you cannot wait if you are hungry.

exercises.hint: Om starts a subordinate clause.
exercises.feedback: After om, inte comes before the verb.
exercises.explanation: Om introduces a subordinate clause, so inte stands before the finite verb är: Om du inte är hungrig kan du vänta.

exercises.source: He is tired because he does not sleep.
answers: Han är trött eftersom han inte sover.
Han är trött eftersom inte han sover.
mistakes.why: Inte has jumped in front of the subject. In a subordinate clause it sits between the subject and the finite verb.

exercises.hint: Eftersom starts a subordinate clause.
exercises.feedback: In the eftersom clause, inte comes before sover.
exercises.explanation: Eftersom introduces a subordinate clause, so inte goes before the finite verb: eftersom han inte sover.

mistakes.why: This is the English order (I never drink). In a Swedish main clause the adverb follows the verb.

exercises.hint: Aldrig sits where inte would.
exercises.feedback: Main clause: the adverb follows the verb.
exercises.explanation: Aldrig takes the place of inte, right after the finite verb: Jag dricker aldrig kaffe.

mistakes.why: That is main-clause order. In the att clause ofta goes before the verb, just as inte would.

exercises.hint: Is this a main clause or an att clause?
exercises.feedback: In a subordinate clause the adverb comes before the verb.
exercises.explanation: The att clause is subordinate, so ofta, like inte, goes before the finite verb: att han ofta jobbar hemma.

exercises.instruction: Fill in the gap with the two words given, in the right order.

mistakes.why: Alltid before the verb follows English (she always is). In a Swedish main clause the verb comes first.

exercises.hint: Treat alltid like inte.
exercises.feedback: Verb first, then alltid.
exercises.explanation: In a main clause alltid takes the slot of inte, after the finite verb: Hon är alltid trött.

mistakes.why: Också stands before the verb, as also does in English. In a Swedish main clause it follows the verb.

exercises.hint: Also is också, in the inte slot.
exercises.feedback: Också comes after talar.
exercises.explanation: Också behaves like inte: in a main clause it follows the finite verb: Jag talar också svenska.

exercises.instruction: Add ofta to the sentence. Write the whole sentence.

mistakes.why: Ofta stands before the verb, which is the order of a subordinate clause.

exercises.hint: Ofta goes where inte would.
exercises.feedback: Put ofta after äter.
exercises.explanation: In a main clause ofta follows the finite verb, exactly like inte: Vi äter ofta fisk.

alternatives.message: Correct too. The usual place for ofta is the inte slot, right after the verb: Vi äter ofta fisk.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged: aldrig still stands before the verb, as in English.

exercises.hint: Where would inte go?
exercises.feedback: Aldrig follows the finite verb in a main clause.
exercises.explanation: Lyssnar is the finite verb of a main clause, so aldrig follows it: Lars lyssnar aldrig på musik.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence. Start with Idag.
exercises.source: These days she is never at home.

mistakes.why: Aldrig before the subject puts stress on hon. Normally it follows the subject.
After Idag the verb must come before the subject.

exercises.hint: Start with Idag: verb, subject, then the adverb.
exercises.feedback: After inversion, aldrig follows the subject.
exercises.explanation: Idag fills first place, so är comes second, then hon, and aldrig sits where inte would, after the subject: Idag är hon aldrig hemma.

mistakes.why: Han is the subject form. After ser you need the object form.
Inte before the verb is subordinate-clause order.

exercises.hint: Honom is a short unstressed pronoun.
exercises.feedback: An object pronoun slips in before inte.
exercises.explanation: With one verb, the unstressed pronoun honom goes before inte: Jag ser honom inte idag.

mistakes.why: Inte before the verb is the subordinate-clause order. This is a main clause.

exercises.hint: Filmen is a noun, not a pronoun.
exercises.feedback: A noun object stays after inte.
exercises.explanation: Filmen is a noun, so it does not move: verb, inte, object: Jag ser inte filmen.

exercises.instruction: Fill in the word for her.

mistakes.why: Hon is the subject form (she). After känner you need the object form.

exercises.hint: Which word means her here?
exercises.feedback: The pronoun object comes before inte.
exercises.explanation: Henne is a short object pronoun, so it slips in before inte: Jag känner henne inte.

mistakes.why: Veta means to know a fact. For knowing a person Swedish uses känna.
Inte has gone before the verb; in a main clause it follows the verb and the pronoun.

exercises.hint: Know a person is känna.
exercises.feedback: Put the pronoun honom before inte.
exercises.explanation: With one verb, the unstressed pronoun goes before inte: Jag känner honom inte. Jag känner inte honom is also heard, mostly with stress on honom.

exercises.instruction: Make the sentence negative with inte. Write the whole sentence.

alternatives.message: Correct when dem is stressed (not them, but others). The everyday order is pronoun, then inte.

mistakes.why: Inte stands before the verb, which is subordinate-clause order.

exercises.hint: Dem is an unstressed pronoun.
exercises.feedback: The pronoun stays before inte.
exercises.explanation: Dem is a short object pronoun, so inte comes after it: Jag hjälper dem inte.

mistakes.why: That is the sentence unchanged: the pronoun has jumped forward although there are two verbs.
Inte must follow the first verb, har, not stand at the end.

exercises.hint: There are two verbs here.
exercises.feedback: With two verbs, the pronoun cannot jump before inte.
exercises.explanation: The pronoun moves before inte only when there is one verb. With har sett the order is har inte sett honom.

alternatives.message: Possible when henne is stressed (not her, but someone else). The everyday order is pronoun, then inte.

mistakes.why: Hon is the subject form; after hör you need the object form.

exercises.feedback: The pronoun goes before inte.
exercises.explanation: With one verb, the unstressed pronoun henne comes before inte: Jag hör henne inte.
